subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The shells
hotspots.description: The two ring layers around the nucleus are the electron shells — layers of space at fixed distances where electrons orbit.
hotspots.positionHint: The two concentric translucent rings around the sodium nucleus.
hotspots.function: Shows the shell layers around the nucleus.

hotspots.label: Inner shell
hotspots.description: The shell closest to the nucleus holds at most 2 electrons. It fills first, before the outer shell.
hotspots.positionHint: The inner ring with its two small electron dots.

hotspots.label: Outermost shell
hotspots.description: The outer shell holds the valence electrons. Sodium's single outer electron makes it eager to bond — this shell decides the chemistry.
hotspots.positionHint: The outer ring with its single electron dot.
hotspots.function: Shows the outermost shell that drives bonding.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A sodium atom floats centered with two clear shell rings, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: soft muted violet; shell rings: thin translucent hairline circles; inner electrons: small dim teal dots; outer electron: larger, brighter teal. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / slate / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Nucleus: soft muted violet matte, roughness ~0.5. Shell rings: translucent hairline circles, alpha ~0.25. Inner electrons: small dim teal dots, roughness ~0.5. Outer electron: larger brighter teal dot, roughness ~0.4. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a sodium atom with its electron shells, built to be read as 'organized layers of electrons — the outer layer does the chemistry.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a ball model of a sodium atom — soft muted violet nucleus (radius ~0.5) at center, two thin translucent hairline shell rings at radii ~0.9 (inner) and ~1.4 (outer). Two small dim teal electron dots (radius ~0.06) on the inner ring; ONE larger brighter teal electron dot (radius ~0.09) on the outer ring. Rings are full circles in the equatorial plane.

2) FILL ORDER (toggleable layer): a small dim dot appears on the inner ring and the app animates electrons filling inner positions first (2 dots), then the outer dot appearing last — showing inner-first filling.

3) REACTIVITY (toggleable layer): a soft highlight rings the outer electron while a small calm neon icon (a full outer shell of 8 dots) floats beside the atom for contrast — reactive lonely electron versus inert full shell.

Camera: framed so both shells and the nucleus fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 5-9k triangles. Named nodes: SodiumNucleus, ShellRing_Inner, ShellRing_Outer, InnerElectrons_02, OuterElectron_01, NeonCompareIcon, NeonShellDots_08. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
